title: jitter isolation probe log (gideon)
content:
Context:
- Quick personal probe while debugging intermittent 95th->99th jump seen in canary last week (region-us-west-2, model: redwood-v1-quant).
- Upstream symptom: p95 stable ~95ms, p99 spikes to ~450–900ms with occasional 2s outliers during brief ingress surges (~1–2s windows).

Hypothesis / goals:
- Isolate whether jitter is: a) KV-cache cold-activation, b) batch packing variability, c) CPU-side GC / Python task stall, or d) network retransmits at proxy layer.
- Measure how much p99 shifts when we (1) force warm-KV hits, (2) constrain batching to fixed sizes, (3) add small request padding to avoid micro-coalescing.

Experiment matrix (short):
- Baseline (A): normal canary profile traffic generator (zipf alpha=1.1, mean QPS 120, bursty short tails).
- Warm-KV (B): pre-prime prefixes for each model shard; target KV hit ~98%.
- Fixed-batch (C): server-side: enforce batch_max_tokens = 512, min_batch_delay_ms = 0 (so small fixed batches).
- Padding (D): client pads to fixed token length (adds 8 tokens to short requests) to reduce batch-size variance.
- Isolated CPU (E): run same workload on instance with pinned cores and stripped background processes.

Test config / commands:
- harness: local runner (bench-runner v0.9.2) using grpc streaming to proxy (proxy v2.3.1).
- ramp: warm-up 5m, run 20m steady with injected microbursts: every 90s, a 3s 2x-QPS spike.
- sample: p50/p75/p90/p95/p99/99.9 + throughput and per-request batch_size, kv_hit bool.

Representative commands (for my notes):
- ./bench-runner --config experiments/jitter-isolation.yaml --target proxy.us-west-2:443 --duration 20m --sample-interval 5s
- curl -X POST $PROXY/debug/kv/prime -d '{"prefixes":... }' # prime for B

Quick raw results (aggregated, median over 3 runs each):
- A (Baseline): p50=48ms, p90=86ms, p95=102ms, p99=620ms, p99.9=1320ms, throughput=118 qps, kv_hit_rate=~56%, median_batch=3
- B (Warm-KV): p50=46ms, p90=84ms, p95=98ms, p99=170ms, p99.9=310ms, throughput=120 qps, kv_hit_rate=98%, median_batch=3
- C (Fixed-batch): p50=52ms, p90=95ms, p95=120ms, p99=220ms, p99.9=420ms, throughput=115 qps, kv_hit_rate=55%, median_batch=2 (forced)
- D (Padding): p50=50ms, p90=88ms, p95=105ms, p99=210ms, p99.9=400ms, throughput=116 qps, kv_hit_rate=60%, median_batch=4
- E (Isolated CPU): p50=44ms, p90=80ms, p95=93ms, p99=160ms, p99.9=290ms, throughput=121 qps, kv_hit_rate=57%, median_batch=3

Observations / interpretation:
- Warm-KV (B) shows the biggest reduction in p99 from baseline (620ms -> 170ms). Strong signal that KV-cache cold misses are a major contributor to long tails.
- Fixed-batch (C) increased p95/p99 moderately; forcing smaller batches slightly reduces throughput and raises p95 (expected overhead), but p99 still much better than baseline — suggests some spikes are due to variable packing delays.
- Padding (D) reduced p99 significantly relative to baseline but not as much as explicit priming; padding increases typical batch sizes (median_batch 4 vs 3) which smooths latency.
- CPU isolation (E) gave small gains: some outliers are CPU-contention/host-noise, but not the dominant source.

Per-request trace snippets (note):
- Baseline long-tail example: request id 83521 -> queue wait 1.1s (batch assembly), server-side kv-miss triggered remote fetch (200–300ms), decode ran, downstream client backpressure observed.
- Warm-KV long-tail example rarely shows >200ms unless coalescing created a big batch during microburst.

Anomalies and oddities:
- A handful of p99 events in B still had >600ms. Digging in traces: those coincide with a 2–3s microburst where batch size shot to 18 (rare) causing long assembly delays + model-level memory pressure causing a 300ms GC-like stall.
- Proxy logs occasionally show 502/timeout retries during heavy bursts which correlate with highest p99s. Need to correlate proxy-side retransmit windows.

Mini conclusions / heuristics:
1) KV priming (or a very inexpensive local negative-cache indicator) pays off for tail reduction. If we can keep kv-hit >95% in the hot path, p99 drops ~3–4x.
2) Batch variance is a tail amplifier. Approaches: encourage slightly larger steady batches (padding), introduce soft upper bound on batch assembly time (max-wait 8ms), or cap batch size to avoid huge packings at burst peaks.
3) Host-level noise contributes but is secondary. CPU pinning and light housekeeping helps but doesn't remove tail alone.
4) Proxy retransmits amplify visible p99s — fix path: instrument and add faster failover/backoff at the proxy layer.

Immediate next steps (practical):
- (A) Prod experiment: deploy KV priming script to two canary nodes for 48h and compare p99 delta. (owner: Mira)
- (B) Impl: add cheapKV negative-cache metric (hit/miss w/ttl=200ms) to reduce remote fetch cost on misses. (owner: me / PR linked)
- (C) Hook telemetry: add per-batch assembly-time histogram (server-side) to Console dashboard (dashboard request).
- (D) Proxy: ask infra (Rowan) to surface retransmit/timeout counters in trace logs with request sampling during bursts.

Open questions / reminders:
- How long does primed-KV remain effective under normal churn? I saw primed prefixes degrade to 80% after ~12h in a quick check — need longer window.
- Should we bias scheduler toward min-batch-delay when ingress variance high? Might increase median latency but reduce p99; need SLO tradeoff analysis.
- Any memory/GC signals on model process during the large-batch tail events? Add jemalloc stats and heap sampling for next run.

Quick TODOs (for myself):
- Save raw traces for the biggest outlier run and attach to JIRA-REINF-4123.
- Add experiment variant: Warm-KV + cap-max-batch-size=12 to see combined effect.
- Share summary in #serving-runtime and propose short priming job for canary fleet.

Notes to self (informal):
- If you see p99 >>> p95, first suspect KV cold path. Then check batch assembly histogram.
- Padding trick is cheap and non-invasive — good temporary knob for product where clients can pad.

Appendix (quick ASCII-ish plot of p99 over time for baseline run):
(legend: time buckets every 30s, values normalized to ms)
[  120 160 150 145 140 130 300 680 620 110 135 120    2s spikes -> 700 650 120 110 ]

End of scratchpad.

-- gideon
